style: Second-grade wax crayon on warm white paper. The first-boot image is the maximum level of neatness; later images may be slightly rougher, with occasional backwards letters or numerals. Keep meaningful instructions in Markdown.

images.first-boot-crayon.png: Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: an instructional illustration for the Marine tier of MANET mesh-radio documentation. Make one landscape page containing four clearly separated crayon drawings in a simple 2 by 2 arrangement, read left to right then down. The drawings must look convincingly made by a young child with real wax crayons on warm white paper: wobbly outlines, uneven proportions, scribbled fills that leave paper showing, little overshoots, visible chunky wax texture. Charming, extremely simple and legible, not polished vector art or professional cartoon art. Use the SAME plain olive green rectangular mesh-radio box with two short black antennas in every panel; this is a schematic symbol, not a realistic product. Panel 1: a blue Ethernet cable connects a small home internet router to the green radio. Panel 2: a black cable from a wall power adapter connects to the radio. Panel 3: the radio beside a large simple clock and a curved looping arrow, conveying waiting through restarts while cables stay connected. Panel 4: a close-up of the radio with one GREEN indicator glowing, short repeated green dash marks suggesting a heartbeat blink; the other indicator is dark. Keep plenty of white space between panels so they are visually distinct. Only a small crayon numeral 1, 2, 3, 4 at the top left of each panel; no other text, labels, speech bubbles, logos, checkmarks, watermarks, or faces. No weapons, camouflage, people, helmets, or military imagery. This should look like a child's drawing explaining useful radio setup, not a joke about the reader. Use clear blue for Ethernet, black for power, green for the same radio and the final LED. Output a 1536 by 1024 landscape image if possible.

No cables between radios. Large child crayon title 'RADIOS' at top, with the R drawn backwards and letters at uneven heights. The radio on the right is drawn more wonkily and tilted. Communicate that radios relay to each other. No internet cloud or implied guaranteed coverage.
